title: Complaints of Wrongful Accusation Leading to Investigation of Innocent Parties
what_it_is: Complaints of Wrongful Accusation Leading to Investigation of Innocent Parties

sections.label: False information to Police
sections.summary: Police do not arrest on allegations alone; giving false information is an offence punishable by jail, fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Police do not make arrests based simply on allegations by a complainant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Deliberately giving wrong or false information to mislead the Police is an offence under section 182 of the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: A person who is convicted of such an offence can be jailed for up to a year, fined up to $5,000, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In the past five years, there were, on average, about 200 cases each year of persons providing false information to public servants, including the Police.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In cases where the false report resulted in a significant waste of public resources, offenders may be prosecuted in Court.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The wrongfully accused party may also take up civil suits against those who have willfully or wrongfully provided false information against them.

sections.label: Police arrest grounds assurance
sections.summary: The Police only arrest if they have reason to believe the person committed an arrestable offence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Speaker, Sir, I would like to assure the Member that if and when the Police do decide to make an arrest, it must have grounds to believe that the person is not wrongly accused.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I do not know the specifics of the case that the Member has brought up.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But I want to give the assurance that the Police only go ahead with an arrest if they have reason to believe that the person has committed an offence that is arrestable.
